title: New skill: revalidate-done-tasks — periodic audit that done tasks are still actually done
description: A task's `state: "done"` records a snapshot of what was true when `pr-reviewer`/`pr-decision` last checked it — nothing currently re-checks that claim later. `orchestrate-tasks` only ever moves the board forward, so a later change elsewhere in the codebase (a deleted file, a renamed function, a quietly-removed test) could silently invalidate an earlier 'done' task's checklist claims without anything catching it. Create a new `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks` skill that iterates every task under `docs/tasks/done/`, re-verifies each checklist item still holds against the current repository state (referenced files/functions still exist and do what the checklist claims), confirms the project's full test suites + coverage gates still pass overall (one full run is enough evidence for all done tasks, not a per-task re-run), and reports any task whose done-claim no longer holds — without silently fixing anything itself, matching the project's existing read-only-audit-agent pattern (e.g. `architecture-reviewer`, `elder-signal-reviewer`).

checklist.step: Design the audit's scope/mechanism — e.g. dispatching `task-qa-reviewer` once per done task vs. a single lighter-weight direct pass — and record the choice with rationale as a `decisions` entry, weighing thoroughness against the cost of potentially dispatching dozens of subagents on every run.
Create `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` implementing the chosen approach, following existing skill file conventions.

Decide what the skill does with a task it finds no longer holds — most consistent with the project's existing rules is to flag it (revert `state` away from `done`, record a `decisions`/`questions` entry explaining why) rather than attempt an autonomous fix, matching the pipeline's existing philosophy of tracking findings on the board rather than an audit silently rewriting code — record as a `decisions` entry.
Register the new skill in CLAUDE.md's Skills list.
Run it once for real against the current (fully-done) board as a smoke test and report what it found (ideally nothing, confirming the board is currently accurate) before considering this done.

Fix the 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section (SKILL.md lines 36-45): it never says how to actually persist a flag given main's branch-protection ruleset rejects every direct push (CLAUDE.md). Every other task-board-writing agent in the project (task-worker: 'Never push directly to main', explicit branch/push/PR workflow) spells this out; this skill's steps 1-4 just git-mv and edit files with no commit/branch/PR mechanics, so following them literally on a main checkout leaves an unpersisted (or push-rejected) change. Add the missing branch/commit/push/PR steps, or otherwise state the intended persistence path explicitly.

Fix step 1 (SKILL.md line 18) / the test-suite step (line 26-30): neither instructs verifying the working tree is on an up-to-date `main` before enumerating done tasks, spot-checking file/function references, or running the test+coverage suites that are reported as 'shared evidence'. Given CLAUDE.md notes the shared working tree can be left on an arbitrary PR branch after a prior agent run, running this skill without first confirming/fetching latest `main` risks the audit's conclusions (clean pass, or a specific flagged task) being computed against the wrong code. Add an explicit 'fetch and check out latest main first' step.

decisions.decision: The skill's default mechanism is a single lightweight direct pass over all docs/tasks/done/*.json files — scripted existence checks for files/functions each checklist item names, plus one full run of the backend and frontend test+coverage suites shared as evidence for every done task — rather than dispatching task-qa-reviewer once per done task. A full task-qa-reviewer dispatch (its own test run, coverage run, and browser walkthrough per task) is reserved as an optional deeper dive the skill can suggest for one specific task the lightweight pass flags as suspicious, not run by default for all ~78 done tasks.
decisions.rationale: Dispatching task-qa-reviewer per done task was rejected as the default: at the board's current scale (~78 done tasks) that means ~78 full subagent runs — each with its own pytest/coverage/vitest invocation and, for UI-facing tasks, its own Playwright browser walkthrough — every time this skill runs. That cost makes the skill impractical to actually run periodically, which defeats its purpose (catching regressions in done work before they go unnoticed indefinitely). The lightweight pass still catches the specific failure mode this skill exists for (a referenced file/function silently disappearing, or a suite-wide regression) by running the real test suites once as shared evidence and spot-checking checklist claims directly against the repo, while keeping a full run tractable. This mirrors an existing pattern already used elsewhere in the project: check-coverage (cheap, broad status check) vs. test-90 (expensive, targeted fix pass), and architecture-reviewer/elder-signal-reviewer (targeted audits) vs. a full task-qa-reviewer re-verification.

decisions.decision: When the skill finds a done task whose checklist claim no longer holds, it never edits application code itself. It flags the task: git mv the task file back out of docs/tasks/done/ to docs/tasks/<id>.json, set state to "implementing" (clear code regression a task-worker can pick up) or "waiting_input" with a questions entry (genuine ambiguity, e.g. unclear whether the referenced behavior was deliberately removed elsewhere), append a decisions or questions entry describing exactly what broke with evidence, and mirror both state and path in docs/tasks/index.json in the same change.
decisions.rationale: Matches the project's existing read-only-audit-agent pattern (architecture-reviewer, elder-signal-reviewer, task-qa-reviewer all report/flag rather than fix) and the task-board philosophy of tracking findings on the board itself rather than a background process silently rewriting code no one asked it to touch. Rejected alternative: having the skill attempt an autonomous fix for simple cases (e.g. a renamed file) — rejected because even a 'simple' rename can hide a deliberate deeper change the skill has no way to distinguish from an accidental break, and CLAUDE.md's whole task-board model routes fixes through task-worker/PR/review, not a silent direct commit from an audit pass.

decisions.decision: The checklist's final smoke-test step was run as a full pass over all 78 docs/tasks/done/*.json files (not a sample): (1) index.json state/path mirror-consistency check across all 81 tasks — clean, no drift; (2) a scripted regex pass extracting every file-path-shaped and function-call-shaped string across all 78 done tasks' checklist text (114 path refs, 64 function refs) and checking each still exists/is defined in the repo — 4 apparent misses, all confirmed by manual follow-up to be false positives of the regex (two are checklist prose referencing another task's JSON file that has itself since moved into docs/tasks/done/, i.e. a stale literal path to a still-valid logical id-pointer per CLAUDE.md's own note on this; one is a checklist item verifying a value against docs/Analyse.md rather than an open 'decide X' judgment call, already explicitly reasoned through in that task's own review/pr_decision notes; one is an external SQLAlchemy library method (Session.get_bind()) mentioned in review prose, not an in-repo symbol; one is descriptive prose ('_wave_showed_state') paraphrasing behavior rather than naming a real function, and the actual underlying code path (evaluate_wave) was confirmed to still exist); (3) one full backend suite run (pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90: 493 passed, 99.84% coverage) and one full frontend suite run (vitest run --coverage: 35 files/205 tests passed, 99.71% lines) as the shared regression evidence. No task was reopened — the board's ~78 done tasks currently hold up.
decisions.rationale: A full pass across the entire done-task set (rather than a sample) was feasible within this session because the checks are scripted/batched rather than per-task manual reads, exactly as the skill itself is designed to work — so this smoke test doubles as direct evidence the mechanism is efficient enough to actually run at full board scale, not just evidence the board is clean today.

decisions.decision: Fixed both blocking review gaps directly in SKILL.md. (1) Persistence: 'Handling a task that no longer holds' now cuts one branch per revalidation run (`audit/revalidate-<YYYY-MM-DD>`, covering every task that run reopens rather than one branch per task), commits the git-mv'd task file(s) + index.json mirror together, pushes, and opens a PR via `gh pr create` describing what broke per task. That PR is explicitly a direct board-authoring PR the invoking human reviews and merges themselves — the same precedent already used this session for PRs #60 and #91 (board/task-board-entry changes with no application code, so the task-worker/pr-reviewer/pr-decision/pr-merger pipeline doesn't apply) — rather than requiring the full 4-agent pipeline for a bookkeeping-only change. Also added the missing timestamp-capture instruction (`date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`) and a note on leaving stale `review`/`pr_decision` fields on a reopened task untouched but calling out the regression explicitly in the new `decisions`/`questions` entry — both were filed as non-blocking follow-ups by pr-reviewer but were small enough to fold into this same fix pass rather than leaving them for the separate followups task. (2) Staleness: added a new step 0 requiring `git status` (abort if another agent appears mid-flight) then `git fetch origin && git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main` (or an equivalent confirm-already-current check) before any enumeration, spot-check, or suite run, and cross-referenced it from the test-suite step.
decisions.rationale: One branch per run (not per task) was chosen over a branch per reopened task because a single revalidation pass produces one coherent finding-set best reviewed as a unit; splitting it into N PRs for N reopened tasks would multiply human review overhead for a bookkeeping-only change with no application code. Reusing the #60/#91 direct-PR precedent (skip the full task-worker/pr-reviewer/pr-decision/pr-merger pipeline) was chosen over running this skill's own findings back through that pipeline because there's no code for those agents to meaningfully review here — the review comment itself only asked that persistence be documented, not that a heavier mechanism be invented; a human merging a small, readable board diff directly is the existing, working pattern for this exact category of change. Folding the two non-blocking timestamp/stale-field follow-ups into this same edit (rather than leaving them purely to the separate `-followups` task) was a low-cost opportunistic fix since it was the same section of the same file already being edited for the blocking items; the followups task itself is left as-is since pr-reviewer already filed it and it may cover additional non-blocking items beyond these two.

comments.summary: Verified both blocking findings from the prior needs_work round are actually fixed, by reading the current SKILL.md rather than trusting the task-worker's report: (1) persistence — 'Handling a task that no longer holds' steps 1-7 now cut one `audit/revalidate-<YYYY-MM-DD>` branch per run, commit the git-mv'd task file(s) + index.json mirror, push, and open a direct board-authoring PR via `gh pr create` (explicitly following the #60/#91 direct-PR precedent, both independently confirmed as real merged PRs of that kind); (2) staleness — new step 0 requires `git status` (abort if another agent looks mid-flight) then `git fetch origin && git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main` before any enumeration, spot-check, or suite run, cross-referenced from the test-suite step. Both fixes hold up as written.

Checked the task-worker's claim of 'opportunistically folding in two of three non-blocking follow-ups' against actual SKILL.md text: step 4 now has the real-timestamp instruction (`date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`) and step 5 now has the stale-review/pr_decision guidance — both confirmed present, matching follow-up items 1 and 2. The third (shared-working-tree coordination caveat) is substantially but not fully covered as a side effect of the new step 0's mid-flight git-status guard — it doesn't extend CLAUDE.md's 'one agent at a time' rule to name this skill, and only catches an agent with an already-uncommitted diff, not one merely reading/testing mid-flight with a clean tree.

Bookkeeping fix applied to docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json as part of this re-review (per the finding above): checklist items 1 and 2 marked done: true (already resolved in SKILL.md, previously left claiming open work); item 3 left open but its text updated to describe the narrower residual gap instead of restating the now-largely-addressed original concern; a decisions entry records the reasoning. Two further non-blocking findings from this re-review's own code-review pass were also added there rather than left only in this PR comment: a same-day `audit/revalidate-<YYYY-MM-DD>` branch-name collision on a second same-day run, and a residual staleness window between step 0's checkout and the later branch cut in 'Handling a task that no longer holds' (which happens only after the potentially multi-minute test-suite run, without re-confirming main is still current).

Re-ran both full suites on the checked-out PR branch: backend `pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=90` — 493 passed, 99.84% coverage (gate 90%); frontend `vitest run --coverage` — 35 test files / 205 tests passed, 99.71% lines / 99.64% branches. Identical to the prior round's numbers, as expected — no application code changed between rounds (diff is still confined to `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` + task-board JSON + CLAUDE.md's one-line skill registration). No backend lint/type-checker is configured (confirmed via `backend/pyproject.toml`); frontend `eslint .` and `tsc -b` both ran clean.

No API route/schema touched (backend/openapi.json correctly untouched); no frontend component added/changed; no new application module/dependency/layer, so a formal architecture-review pass doesn't apply. No UI-facing surface in this PR (pure skill/doc/task-board change) — browser walkthrough explicitly not applicable, not silently skipped. Decisions cross-check: all checklist items phrased as a judgment call (the original three, plus the two 'fix the blocking gap' items added by the prior review) have corresponding decisions entries with rationale. No `pr_decision` field exists on this task (confirmed by direct inspection, not just the prior review's own note), so there is nothing stale to clear from this pass either.

review.notes: PR #92 accepted on re-review. Both blocking findings from the prior needs_work round are genuinely fixed and hold up against a direct read of the current SKILL.md, not just the task-worker's self-report: persistence mechanics (branch/commit/push/direct-PR, matching the real #60/#91 precedent) and a staleness guard (step 0's git-status mid-flight check + fetch/checkout/pull of main) are both now present and executable as documented. Full backend (493 passed, 99.84% coverage) and frontend (205 passed, 99.71% lines) suites re-run clean, matching the prior round exactly since no application code changed; no lint/type-check regression; no API/schema/OpenAPI or frontend-component surface to check; no UI-facing surface, so the browser walkthrough is explicitly not applicable rather than skipped. A `code-review` pass surfaced one bookkeeping gap and two further minor, non-blocking robustness gaps in the skill's own mechanics — all three fixed/tracked directly on docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json as part of this same review (two follow-up items marked done as already resolved, one narrowed to its real residual gap, two new items added), rather than only living in this PR comment. None of the three rise to blocking: the bookkeeping gap is a stale checklist entry (not incorrect skill behavior), and the two skill-mechanics gaps are narrow edge cases (same-day rerun branch collision; a small staleness window between step 0's checkout and a later branch cut after a multi-minute suite run) in a workflow doc that a human reviews before any board edit actually lands, not a silent-failure path.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran both full suites on the checked-out PR branch: backend pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90 -> 493 passed, 99.84% coverage; frontend vitest run --coverage -> 35 files/205 tests passed, 99.71% lines/99.64% branches — exact match to pr-reviewer's reported numbers. Confirmed via `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` that the diff is confined to .claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md (1-line registration), and docs/tasks/* board JSON — no application code touched. Read the full SKILL.md diff directly and verified both previously-blocking fixes are actually present as text: step 0's git-status/fetch/checkout/pull-main staleness guard, and the 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section's branch/commit/push/gh-pr-create persistence steps (1-7). Cross-checked docs/tasks/index.json against the actual filesystem (docs/tasks/done/skill-revalidate-done-tasks.json and docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json both exist exactly where index.json's path fields say) — no mirror drift. Confirmed no stale pr_decision existed on this task before this write (avoiding the known merge-ordering pitfall), and this confirmed_at postdates review.reviewed_at (18:22:53Z).
